text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Politicians covered up a scandal surrounding the privatisation of Savings Bank at the end of 1995 at the peak of a banking crisis. The newspaper alleges that companies which took part in the partial privatisation of the bank bought shares for the chairman in return for favourable treatment. The newspaper alleges that politicians including President Algirdas Brazauskas knew of the transactions but suppressed the information.
- Lithuania is ready to lead the way in the integration process into NATO, Defence Minister Ceslovas Stankevicius said during a meeting with U.S. defence and security experts in Vilnius.
- December's average salary was 774 litas, an 11.8 percent rise against November, the statistics department says.
- The real growth of the Lithuanian stock market has only just started, dealers say.
- Out of 58 HIV-infected people, 33 live in Klaipeda, and some experts say it is the beginning of an epidemic.
- Commercial bank assets rose by 55 percent or 1.9 billion litas over the last three years, the central bank said. Assets of 11 banks were estimated at 5.4 billion litas at end 1996.
- Lithuanian ambassadors gathered in Vilnius for their annual three-day meeting.
- The interior affairs minister is dissatisfied with the work of the boarder police.

- In a surprise move, Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius plans to appoint Rimantas Ziemelis, a professor from Kaunas with no earlier connection to oil business, to be the head of the newly-created national oil firm Lietuvos Nafta, the newspaper's sources say.

- Lithuania was granted a BB plus credit rating by European agency IBCA, shared also by Russia, but the country did not succeed to climb as high as Latvia, which was granted an investment grade BBB- rating by Standard & Poors.
- The list of filling stations in Lithuania in January was headed by Lietuvos Kuras which has 130. Lukoil Baltija has 27, Lietuva Statoil 11, Shell Lietuva 10 and Neste Oil seven filling stations.
